classification.difficultyReason: Infer the outer diameter from two tangent inner circles, then subtract both inner areas.

content.prompt: Find the shaded area of the figure below, leaving your answer in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Two unequal unshaded circles lie side by side on the horizontal diameter of a larger circle. The inner circles touch each other and the outer circle at its opposite diameter endpoints. Light purple identifies the requested remaining region; ordinary source blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: Inner diameters are 14 cm and 10 cm. Their collinear diameters together form the outer diameter. Relative radii are 7:5:12, with exact internal and mutual tangencies.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the printed diameter givens are visible; no inferred dimensions or area answers are supplied.

answer.short:
$70\pi\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the areas of both inner circles from the area of the outer circle.
answer.worked:
The inner diameters together form the outer diameter.

$$\begin{align*}d_{\text{outer}}&=14+10=24\text{ cm}\\r_{\text{outer}}&=24\div2=12\text{ cm}\\r_{\text{left}}&=14\div2=7\text{ cm}\\r_{\text{right}}&=10\div2=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=\pi(12)^2-\pi(7)^2-\pi(5)^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=(144-49-25)\pi\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=70\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
